title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: usage-based billing models in the model selector
notes: claim 58: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing omits the required Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription licence and presents credit requests as part of the initial rollout, contrary to Microsoft's notice. It also confuses discovery with access, overstates data-boundary protections, and supplies an incomplete Graph call and incorrect control documentation.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.claim: The release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: General Availability is listed for December CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"

claims.claim: Preview is listed for November CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platforms are Desktop and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on November 4, 2026.
Microsoft plans access to usage-based billing models from the Chat model selector.
claims.quote: Users will be able to access models that require usage-based billing (UBB) from the model selector in Chat.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Tenant administrators must allocate credits before users can interact with these models.
claims.quote: Tenant admins will need to allocate credits so that users can interact with these models.

claims.claim: Users can request additional credits within the experience when the model-selector feature initially rolls out.
claims.quote: After the initial rollout, we plan to roll out the ability for users to request additional credits from their tenant admin.
claims.fix: Separate model access from credit requests: MC1519122 says in-product requests are planned after the initial rollout, without a date. Tell users the organisation's interim request process. Cite MC1519122 and report its Frontier window, early to mid-November 2026, and Worldwide GA window, early to mid-December 2026.

claims.claim: Frontier-model usage is charged in Copilot Credits beyond the everyday AI covered by the per-user subscription.
claims.quote: UBB is used for advanced AI and frontier models, extending beyond the everyday AI included in the USL.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/user-subscription-license-usage-based-billing to sources for the USL/UBB distinction and fixed-price licensing discussion.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The feature requires administrator opt-in before users can use UBB models.
claims.quote: Users will not have access to UBB models unless UBB is enabled.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Consumption licensing and a variable cost rating describe the Copilot Credits meter.
claims.quote: Microsoft's usage-based billing model charges customers based on actual usage, measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The usage-based billing framework supports pay-as-you-go, Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plan (P3), and existing prepaid capacity packs.
claims.quote: Enable usage-based billing with flexible options including Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3), pay-as-you-go, or existing prepaid capacity packs.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Credit rates for this Chat model-selector feature are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat usage based billing model selector GPT-6 Astra Claude Fable 5.1 Copilot Credits rates USL; Copilot Chat model credit rates Astra. Opened USL/UBB, billing overview, setup and billing comparison; no Chat model-selector rates found.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat users need only enabled UBB and a covering spending policy to be in scope.
claims.quote: Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL) with UBB enabled
claims.fix: Add the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription licence prerequisite to Scope and licensing.notes. State that UBB and allocated credits are additional requirements, not a replacement for the USL; cite MC1519122 and https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/user-subscription-license-usage-based-billing.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Without a spending policy users cannot see the models, so creating no policy hides them.
claims.quote: In short, this setting controls visibility, while Cost Management under the Copilot node in the Microsoft 365 admin center controls access and spending.
claims.fix: Replace the visibility guarantee with 'Without enabled UBB and allocated credits, users cannot use these models.' Explain that discovery and access requests are separate controls and that the cited discovery setting is deprecated. Keep the Chat-specific hidden-versus-disabled appearance as an open question.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: Spending policies allocate or reserve a user's credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.
claims.fix: Preserve the roadmap's requirement that admins allocate credits, but describe spending policies precisely as access and spending-limit controls, not reserved credit allocations. Replace 'allocate credits through spending policies' with 'enable UBB, provide credits and configure access and limits through spending policies'.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The existing Cost Management experience lets administrators manage credit requests.
claims.quote: Administrators use the Cost management dashboard in the Microsoft 365 admin center to govern access, establish spending controls, manage credit requests, and monitor consumption.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can configure custom credit-request routing.
claims.quote: Configure request-routing policies for supported credit requests.

claims.claim: Without custom routing policies credit requests land on a default administrator audience.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot credit requests request routing policies default administrators Credit requests tab; Copilot credit requests default administrators. Opened billing overview, setup, manage credits and monitor spending; none identifies the claimed default recipient audience.
claims.fix: Replace with the documented narrower statement: 'Requests that do not match a custom request policy continue through the Microsoft credit request service and can be resolved in the Microsoft 365 admin center.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Identity-based policies control access for users and groups.
claims.quote: Control which users and groups can access supported services using identity-based policies.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go credit usage is billed to a connected Azure subscription.
claims.quote: If you choose to override by using the pay-as-you-go option, the connected Azure subscription is billed on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.claim: P3 is an annual commitment.
claims.quote: Copilot Credit pre-purchase plans provide discounted commit units for eligible Copilot Credit usage during a one-year term.

claims.claim: P3 provides discounts compared with pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: Pre-purchasing annual credits provides discounted rates compared to pay-as-you-go pricing.

claims.claim: Usage beyond P3 credits continues on pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: The process uses available pre-purchase credits first, and once they're exhausted, usage automatically continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Policy-level and optional user-level limits constrain credit spending.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Administrators can set threshold alerts before spending limits are reached.
claims.quote: You can set the threshold as a credit amount or a percentage.

claims.claim: Dashboard totals can be point-in-time views.
claims.quote: Dashboard totals and exports might be point-in-time views and can refresh at different intervals.

claims.claim: Cost Management usage views express amounts in credits rather than currency.
claims.quote: Everything in this view is expressed in Copilot Credits, not currency.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management shows billed amounts for the connected Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Use Azure Cost Management and Azure billing views to understand billed charges for the Azure subscription connected to your billing method.

claims.claim: Global Administrators and Billing Administrators can configure billing methods.
claims.quote: Global administrator and Billing administrator roles can add, select, and change billing methods, and set billing methods in policies.

claims.claim: AI Administrators and License Administrators can manage policy limits and alerts.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: Supported reader roles can view consumption.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.

claims.claim: Until this change the model behind Microsoft 365 Copilot was Microsoft's choice rather than the user's.
claims.quote: The model selector in Copilot Chat now includes GPT-5.2. Users can pick Quick Response for immediate answers or Think Deeper for more thorough reasoning.
claims.fix: Remove the historical assertion that users previously had no model choice. Say 'This change adds usage-based frontier models alongside existing subscription-covered model choices.'

claims.claim: The Copilot user subscription provides a fixed-price foundation.
claims.quote: The USL covers everyday AI work, providing a fixed-price AI foundation for your workforce.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Usage-based credit consumption varies with the models used and the work performed.
claims.quote: The number of credits a task consumes varies with the models used, the amount of context retrieved, the runtime needed to plan and complete the work, and the tools the task calls.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Model choice does not change the Microsoft 365 data boundary and all prompts and Graph data remain under the same Copilot commitments.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings such as Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary
claims.fix: Remove the blanket boundary assurance from the bullet and risk rationale. State that processing boundaries and contractual terms depend on the selected model and tenant eligibility; Claude models are excluded from EU Data Boundary and applicable in-country processing commitments, and separately enabled Data Retention models use different terms.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Consumption tab reports usage by policy, user, group, agent and service.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab enables detailed analysis by spending policy, user, group, agent, or service.

claims.claim: Spending policies, limits and alerts are configured in Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration.
claims.quote: Select Manage Configuration. The Configuration tab within the Cost management page is displayed.

claims.claim: /beta/copilot/costManagement (Cost Management API) is a documented actionable Graph call for spending policies, limits and alerts.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot pay as you go billing policies Microsoft Graph API PowerShell create billing policy; Copilot billing policy Graph API. Opened Cost Management API overview: it documents /copilot/costManagement as the root, but lists specific child operations, not this methodless call.
claims.fix: Replace the namespace description with an actual operation, for example 'GET /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies', and narrow its description to listing policies. Link the list-spendingPolicies reference from the overview. Add that these beta APIs are subject to change and unsupported in production; do not imply that GET configures limits or alerts.

claims.claim: The cited setup page documents Copilot > Settings > All Settings > Access to usage-based billing experiences.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Settings > All Settings. Select Access to usage-based billing experiences.
claims.fix: The path exists, but not on the cited setup page. Change controls[1].ui.docs, its table link and its source to https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/request-access-usage-based-billing-experiences.

claims.claim: Access to usage-based billing experiences controls who can see UBB experiences.
claims.quote: Your selection controls who can request access. It does not complete the usage-based billing setup by itself.
claims.fix: Rename this control 'Who can request a spending policy for usage-based billing experiences'. State that it governs requests from users without a policy, not model visibility or UBB enablement.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for the UBB access-request setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Access to usage-based billing experiences Settings discovery Graph API; usage-based billing experiences API access. Opened request-access and discovery-setting pages and Cost Management API overview; no equivalent setting API found.

claims.claim: Anthropic access is scoped through Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Anthropic and its user-selection setting.
claims.quote: Under Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences, select your users or groups and Save.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: Anthropic opt-in is portal-only
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an automation equivalent for the Anthropic provider opt-in.
claims.quote: Searched: AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors Graph PowerShell API; Anthropic Microsoft 365 PowerShell setting. Opened connect-to-ai-subprocessor and copilot-anthropic-apps; no provider opt-in API or PowerShell equivalent found.

claims.claim: The capacity-packs page gives Copilot > Billing & usage > Pay-as-you-go services for Copilot billing configuration.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Billing & usage. Select the Pay-as-you-go services tab
claims.fix: Retain the cited legacy path but note the newer commerce documentation also gives Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage > Pay-as-you-go. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/services/pay-as-you-go-setup-copilot and identify this as the classic billing experience.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for the classic Copilot-service pay-as-you-go billing-policy connection is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot pay as you go billing policies Microsoft Graph API PowerShell create billing policy; Copilot billing policy Graph API. Opened capacity-packs and Cost Management API overview; searched setup-pay-as-you-go and commerce setup excerpts. No classic-policy connection API found.

claims.claim: The classic Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go billing-policy connection governs this new UBB model-selector feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat usage based billing model selector GPT-6 Astra Claude Fable 5.1 Copilot Credits rates USL; Copilot Chat model selector hide billing. Opened capacity-packs, USL/UBB and billing overview; none links classic agent billing-policy connections to these models.
claims.fix: Remove the classic billing row from this feature's direct controls, or add a note: 'General Copilot Chat agent-billing control; Microsoft has not confirmed that this classic billing-policy connection governs UBB model-selector access.' Keep UBB enablement and credit requirements anchored to MC1519122.

claims.claim: The linked Manage Copilot Credits page documents approval under Copilot > Cost Management > Credit requests.
claims.quote: From the Top Actions section, you can View requests
claims.fix: Replace with Copilot > Cost Management > Overview > Top Actions > View requests, which opens Credit requests. Link https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending#viewing-and-managing-credit-requests instead of the manage-credits page, which does not supply this path.

claims.where: Governance controls: The model selector itself has no switch
claims.claim: No separate Chat UBB model-selector switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat UBB model selector admin hide models per model limits data boundary model choice history; Copilot Chat model selector hide billing. Opened UBB setup, manage credits, discovery and access-request pages; no separate Chat selector switch found.
claims.fix: Replace the absolute 'The model selector itself has no switch' with 'Microsoft has not documented a separate Chat UBB model-selector switch at the time of writing (November 2026).' Do not extend Cowork-only model templates to Chat.

claims.where: Open questions: Which models will be metered
claims.claim: Which models will be metered in this rollout remains unknown.
claims.quote: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 will be generally available as UBB models with this rollout. Previously communicated eligibility requirements for these models apply.
claims.fix: Name GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 as the models announced in MC1519122, preserving the eligibility qualification. Keep only the unpublished credit rates as the open question and cite the notice.

claims.where: Scope: Government cloud dates not published
claims.claim: Government-cloud rollout dates for this specific UBB model-selector feature are not published in the supplied evidence or located documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat UBB GCC rollout. Read roadmap, MC1519122 and Anthropic region documentation/search excerpts; found general government-cloud and Anthropic announcements but no government-cloud rollout dates for this specific UBB model-selector feature.

claims.claim: Per-model spending limits for Chat UBB models are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat per-model limits billing; Copilot Chat UBB model selector admin hide models per model limits. Opened setup, manage credits and Cost Management API overview; found policy/user limits and Cowork-only templates, not Chat per-model limits.

claims.claim: A spending policy can automatically apply to future supported services.
claims.quote: The Auto-apply new services setting is enabled by default for spending policies. Administrators can turn off the setting for policies where future services and agents should be reviewed before they're added.

claims.where: What's changing: roadmap does not name models or credit rates
claims.claim: The roadmap record itself does not name models or their credit rates.
claims.quote: Users will be able to access models that require usage-based billing (UBB) from the model selector in Chat.

claims.claim: The controls table covers every control the guidance asks administrators to use and every material control gap stated in prose.
claims.quote: Design credit request routing so requests reach a team that can judge them. / Review the Consumption tab weekly during preview / The model selector itself has no switch
claims.fix: Add rows for credit-request review/routing and consumption monitoring, and a both-null row for the undocumented selector-specific switch. For review/routing and monitoring use https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending; distinguish request review from routing automation.

claims.claim: The new model-selector capability is visible to every Copilot Chat user once rolled out.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Chat model selector hide billing; Copilot Chat UBB model selector admin hide models per model limits. Read MC1519122 and discovery/access-request documentation: they describe eligibility and general discovery, not visibility to every Chat user.
claims.fix: Remove 'every Copilot Chat user'. Describe access as limited to eligible Microsoft 365 Copilot USL users with UBB enabled and allocated credits, and do not assert universal model visibility without Chat-specific discovery documentation. Reassess the impact rationale on that qualified scope.
